key_insight: A hybrid MILP–QUBO framework delivers verified routing improvements while identifying a current QAOA hardware boundary of 4 customers per subproblem (16 qubits).
engineering_relevance: Vehicle-level decomposition offers a practical way to test quantum optimization within capacity- and time-window-constrained routing without relying on monolithic QUBO formulations.
method: Combine classical MILP with vehicle-level QUBO route optimization.
Solve QUBOs using Toshiba SQBM+ and QAOA on Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Emerald.
Validate feasibility and accept only improvements over classical baselines.
evidence_signal: Across five London-derived benchmarks with 10–70 customers, SQBM+ reduced verified fleet distance by 2.80% (7,927 m) for 25 customers and 0.22% (1,186 m) for 55 customers.
watch_item: Assignment-level time-window tightness remains the main scalability bottleneck; the reported distance gains come from SQBM+, not evidence of quantum hardware advantage.
paper_title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Optimization for CVRPTW: A Systems Framework with Provable Feasibility and Empirical Hardware Limits
